preamble: Nasalization of open-mid [ɛ] before a nasal consonant is often accompanied by raising to close-mid [ẽ], since many languages contrast fewer heights among nasal than among oral vowels. Horb Swabian neutralizes /i e ɛ/ to [ẽ] before nasals, and Portuguese reflects Vulgar Latin /ɛ/ before a coda nasal as [ẽ], where Italian keeps oral [ɛ].

examples.note: Nasal Raising: /ɛ/ from MHG ë becomes mid-close [ẽ] before a nasal, while it stays [ɛ] elsewhere (brët > [b̥rɛtʰ] 'board').

examples.from: Middle High German hemde 'shirt' (Secondary Umlaut e realized as [ɛ])
examples.note: The same raising applies to [ɛ] from MHG secondary-umlaut e (compare beche > [b̥ɛç] 'brooks').

examples.from: Latin ventus 'wind' (Vulgar Latin /ɛ/, cf. Italian vento /ˈvɛnto/)
examples.note: Before a coda nasal the open-mid vowel is neutralized with close-mid and nasalized; the nasal consonant is absorbed into the vowel.

examples.from: Latin tempus 'time' (Vulgar Latin /ɛ/, cf. Italian tempo /ˈtɛmpo/)

sources: Kniess, T. B. (2025). Nasalization and Nasal Vowels in the Swabian Dialect of Horb: A Phonological Analysis of Kauffmann 1890. PhD dissertation, Indiana University. https://scholarworks.iu.edu/dspace/items/f9ca887d-4125-46c1-8eb0-933b17f7d00c
